title: Carrier-Class Calibration, Seed 80301 — three carriers x two prompts
verdict: Production receipt only. Route identity verified per cell; interpretation belongs to the Molten and Ghost functions.
description: Amendment SS-C.2. Three conditioning arms (clean generic-cat envelope, the demoted "mush" envelope, and a source-ablated blank plate) run under two prompts. The original exterior prompt verbally restates the source morphology; the neutralized prompt removes that restatement and changes nothing else. All six cells verified route-identical except the supplied image and the prompt file.

comparisonClass.knownCoupling: Arm A is produced by a different model family (Z-Image-Turbo photo -> TRELLIS) than arms B and C (Blender envelope compiler), so carrier cleanliness and production route are coupled in that arm. Arm A also carries TRELLIS surface noise (fur tufts) absent from the smooth compiler arms, and its camera is nearer a three-quarter front than the arms’ right-sagittal.

claimCeiling: Claim ceiling: these six fixed-route cells establish prompt-vs-image attribution for posture under this exact route, seed, and prompt pair. They do not establish multi-seed reliability, anatomical fidelity, 3D correspondence, reconstruction quality, carrier ranking, or production admission. Single seed: an existence probe, not a stable effect.

cells.group: Group 1 — ORIGINAL exterior prompt (restates source morphology in words)
cells.promptText: Use the supplied silhouette and proportions as the exact shape guide for one coherent living domestic cat. Keep its low front, folded rear stance, body length, limb spacing, support placement, and direction unchanged. Render a complete continuous fur-covered exterior with natural paws, face, ears, and tail in a neutral three-quarter studio view on a clean pale background. Preserve the source's unusual mass relationships instead of replacing them with a generic cat pose. No cutaway, exposed interior, diagram, text, interface, or logo.
cells.observation: Crouched, low front, head image-left. Closely resembles the source-ablated cell below.
